From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-21T02:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — initial pricing question

Alex — great to hear, thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a concise proposal and an illustrative pricing calc (see attached PDF + spreadsheet). High-level bullets below so you can paste into your procurement packet: 

- Baseline: Hosted API pricing (no commit): $0.0009 / token (generation) / $0.0001 / token (embedding) — typical for this model class.
- Optimize toolkit add-on (features + support for batching/cache/quantized variants): flat $1,200/mo + usage tier credits.
- Commit discounts: 6-mo committed monthly usage (50M tokens/mo) => 18% applied to per-token rate; 12-mo => 25% (pricing example in attached calc).
- Batching/caching credits: provided as a monthly "credits bucket" measured in effective saved tokens. Example: for 50M tokens, we would propose a 6-mo commit include 4M/month of caching credits (applied as token-equivalent offsets before billing). Any additional usage billed at the discounted rate.
- Quantization advisory: included in the Optimize toolkit pilot (we run a quantization assessment + recommended profile — e.g., int8/4-bit tradeoffs). Quantization work can reduce compute by ~20–40% depending on model; we recommend starting with INT8 and a follow-up 4-bit pilot if memory/latency requirements are strict.

Next steps: If procurement is comfortable with a template 6-mo commercial, I can introduce Rishi (commercial lead) and Dev (inference engineer) to lock technical and commercial details.

Attaching: FW-Optimize-Proposal-v1.pdf, pricing_calc.xlsx

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

If you can send a short counter / proposed commercial that maps to a 6-mo commit for 50M tokens/mo (and show post-credit invoice calc), that will speed things up.

Thanks for the summary, Tessa. Proposed commercial structure (keeps overall concession in target band):

- No-commit baseline: standard rates as listed in proposal.
- 6-mo commit (50M tokens/mo): 18% per-token discount + 4M/month caching credits (token-equivalent). One-time onboarding credit = $10,000 (applied against first invoice).
- 12-mo commit (100M tokens/mo): 25% per-token discount + 8M/month caching credits + onboarding credit $25,000 + complimentary quantization assessment (2–3 weeks).

Notes on credits -> billing mechanics (billing language we should use):
"Caching credits are token-equivalent offsets applied to the monthly usage invoice prior to discount calculations. Unused credits do not roll over and expire at the end of each billing month. Credits are non-transferable and limited to usage related to the contracted account."

On the quantization pilot: Dev, can you confirm estimated effort? My assumption: 10–15 engineer-hours for initial assessment + 2–3 days of runtime experiments. If that holds, we can include a free assessment for 12-mo commits and offer a discounted paid pilot for 6-mo commits (we absorb 50% of engineering costs).

Laura: the credit billing phrasing above is intentionally conservative; please flag any legal concerns.

Rishi
